en: Emptying stagnant water in old tires prevents Aedes aegypti mosquitoes from breeding and spreading dengue fever.
Washing hands with soap destroys the lipid envelope of viruses, effectively stopping the spread of infections.
Cooking pork to an internal temperature of 71 degrees Celsius kills Trichinella parasites that cause trichinosis.
Washing a dog bite wound immediately with soap and water reduces the risk of rabies virus transmission.
Brushing teeth twice daily removes sticky plaque bacteria that produce acids responsible for destroying tooth enamel.
Eating wild mushrooms is dangerous because many species contain amatoxins that cause severe, fatal liver damage.
Boiling drinking water for at least one minute kills harmful waterborne bacteria like Vibrio cholerae, which causes cholera.
Wearing long pants and closed shoes in muddy fields protects your skin from parasitic leech bites.
Eating dark leafy vegetables like malunggay provides essential iron, which helps red blood cells carry oxygen.
Wearing a properly fitted helmet while biking absorbs impact forces, protecting the brain from severe traumatic injuries.
Applying sunscreen with SPF 30 or higher blocks ultraviolet B rays, preventing painful sunburns and skin damage.
Dust mites in unwashed bedding release proteins that trigger asthma attacks and allergic reactions in sensitive children.
